wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Iran answered a US strike on Qeshm by hitting Kuwait and Bahrain, which faced 4 Iranian attacks in 6 days, while Iran said mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours and traffic through Hormuz fell 15% in the week to 18 November. In Brooklyn, Asif Merchant received 330 months for plotting to kill Donald Trump.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Tankers were hit off Khasab on consecutive days, Iran blaming one on a mine, and Bahrain reported an Iranian strike as Gharibabadi called the US naval blockade an act of war, yet none of it lifted the price. The earlier shock showed downstream: Lufthansa cut 1,000 jobs over fuel costs, and electric cars took about a third of European sales in October.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August after Trump called a new Iran offensive "highly unlikely" while talks went on, and US crude eased with it. Tanker hits off Khasab, which Iran blamed on mines, lifted prices only briefly, and Russia's crude shipments reached their highest since late July, adding supply.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news came from the Gulf: a mine struck an LNG carrier in Hormuz, only 2 tankers crossed the strait in a week, and the IMF said Qatar's economy would shrink more than 14%. None of it reports on US supply, demand or exports, so it does not by itself account for the price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Everything since the last reading postdates it, so none of it explains the climb: India's wheat sowing trails last year as farmers switch crops, a wheat ship capsized off Bulgaria after a reported sea-drone strike, and Pakistan's flour costs 44.2% more than a year ago, which led Punjab to cap the retail price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: The fortnight's farm news ran on India, where farmers switched crops and cut wheat planting, and on a UN appeal to Iran and the US to let fertilisers through Hormuz. Both postdate the October reading, and neither concerns the rice trade.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Adani agreed to finance Codelco's Kaburkaala exploration in northern Chile, National Resources Limited reported copper and gold at Chagai, and protesters targeted copper mines in Negros and Colombia. All of it came after the latest monthly reading, and none of it explains the price.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts, and the Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes; Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open for December. Yields no longer follow Brent down: inflation has spread from fuel into the wider economy, so cheaper oil has stopped bringing borrowing costs lower.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Nvidia has lost $2.74 trillion in value since the index peaked, and Micron, TSMC and ASML fell with it as investors balked at AI capital spending with no profit in sight. Ten-year Treasuries still yield above 5% and markets are pricing a Fed hike, so the wait for data centres to pay back now costs more.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: Reports that Nvidia's board may oust Jensen Huang knocked its futures down nearly 12%, and an SEC accounting probe then crashed chip stocks; Nvidia alone has shed $2.74 trillion. The AI selloff reached Micron, TSMC and ASML in the same week Anthropic raised a record $81.3bn in its Nasdaq debut.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The fortnight brought a US forecast raising 2027 gasoline and diesel prices, and Russia shipping its most crude since late July after drone strikes on its refineries; neither accounts for the fall at the pump.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Liquefied gas from the Gulf has nearly stopped moving: Bloomberg tracking, reported by TASS, counted 2 LNG carriers through Hormuz in the week to 17 November, after Iran's navy said one hit a mine. A drone attack also suspended production at Iraq's Khor Mor gasfield, and the IEA said $40bn of pipelines will not end the Gulf's Hormuz dependence.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's economic news from Pakistan was about food and trade: wheat flour cost 44.2% more than a year ago, Punjab capped a 10kg bag at Rs1,275, and the Hormuz closure cut mango export earnings from $100 million to $60 million. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's news about Nigeria's money was political, not monetary. Makinde's camp demanded a probe of 11.2 trillion naira in loans backed by 340 million barrels of future crude, and Atiku pledged to review that pledged crude to subsidise petrol. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: IMF staff agreed to release $2.3bn to Egypt, a decree set aside 112 million square metres of Red Sea coast to cut public debt, and the state began paying on the spot for gold from informal miners in Aswan. All three came after the pound had done most of its firming, so none of them explains it.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: The fortnight's news from Turkey carried a 6.4% fall in gold to $3,853 an ounce, which thinned the cushion Turkish savers hold against the lira, but nothing in it accounts for the currency's own slide.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight in Bangladesh brought political strain rather than economic news. Sheikh Hasina applied for a Bangladeshi passport, arsonists hit 37 Grameen Bank branches from 10 November, and the home of Muhammad Yunus was set on fire. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah fell to a record low as bets on the Fed's next move lifted the dollar. The slide came days after a political jolt in Jakarta, when Prabowo was said to have accepted the resignation of his Vice President. The EU governments' sign-off on their trade deal with Indonesia did not turn it.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight brought Lebanon's army seizing a weapons depot in Beirut's southern suburbs, and word that Israel's war left 24% of Lebanon's wheatland in the Bekaa Valley fallow. Nothing reported touched the central bank or the dollar market, and neither story accounts for the rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The fortnight's news about the currency itself was structural: China's central bank said nearly 30% of the country's goods trade is now settled in yuan. Neither that nor the Shenzhen summit of Trump, Putin and Xi accounts for the rate's small drift.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee's firming came as October's trade figures showed exports jumping 30%, which narrowed the monthly trade deficit to $20.09 billion. A smaller gap between what India buys and sells abroad means importers need fewer dollars, so fewer rupees are sold to buy them.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The weeks carried Lula's election win, which Milei pointedly ignored, and a Senate vote in which 45 senators passed the government's fiscal adjustment bill. Neither was reported as moving the currency, and nothing in the news accounts for the real's slide.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso weakened after Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans stopped, a threat set off by 1,500 migrants walking north from Tapachula. Its weakest day came as soldiers captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa, a capture that left eleven dead in the fighting that followed.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Two strains on the euro landed in one week: Washington sold $500 million of euros to buy yen, and France's borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points while the ECB declined to step in, leaving the spread to markets. Protests against energy and food prices pushed up by the Gulf war then spread across French cities.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, and as the currency neared 160 per dollar Washington joined in, selling $500 million of euros for yen. The weakness now bites policy: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans to rein in the next five-year defence budget because much of it buys American weapons priced in dollars.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: TASS reported that Russia's gold reserves had hit a 7-year low, and Trump, Putin and Xi met in Shenzhen as Washington set a January 2027 deadline for a Ukraine peace deal. Talks in Abu Dhabi had stalled earlier in the month. None of it accounts for the ruble's small moves against the dollar.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's Reserve Bank held its repo rate at 7.25%, and 3 of 7 rate-setters voted to hike as inflation risks widened. A hold that hawkish usually supports a currency, and nothing else reported in the fortnight accounts for the rand's weakening.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The slide began with forced selling. MSCI dropped Strategy from its indices, which put that company's bitcoin-buying model on the line, and leveraged positions were liquidated as the price fell. Rate hikes and a tech selloff then drew money out, and BlackRock's bitcoin fund posted a record $541 million outflow.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ether fell with bitcoin, which dropped below $60,000 to a two-year low after the Fed's hikes. Firms that borrowed against coin they hold were squeezed: BTCS told the SEC it cannot rule out liquidation of a $54 million Aave loan backed by its ether. Developers also delayed the Glamsterdam upgrade, which risked breaking 15,000 contracts.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Bets that the Fed would raise rates again, together with a selloff in AI stocks, pushed 'real rates' up, and gold, which pays nothing, lost 8.9% in its worst week since March. Turkish households who keep their savings in gold against the lira lost part of that cushion, and Russia's central bank gold reserves fell to a 7-year low.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: A three-power "peace declaration" from Trump, Xi and Putin in Shenzhen named no war, while Russia hit 2 bridges and the subway in Kyiv. On NATO's edge, a suspected Russian missile burned in a Polish field, Denmark expelled an attaché over a plot to kill Kyivstoner, and Estonia closes all vehicle crossings into Russia on 1 December.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran has kept the strait shut, with Rezaei saying it stays closed until Iran's seven conditions are met. Projectiles hit tankers off Khasab on consecutive days, though none of the 30-plus claimed mine hits has been verified, and only 2 liquefied natural gas tankers crossed last week as a single transit cost $64m to insure.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi called the US naval blockade an act of war and vowed to break it, while projectiles hit tankers on consecutive days off Khasab and Iran blamed a mine. Qatar's LNG shipments all but stopped, and the IMF said Qatar's economy will shrink more than 14% this year.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Yemen's government forces withdrew from the strait on 15 November and left the Houthis holding its coast. The same day, a Japanese container ship transited it for the first time in three years. The Houthis have since pushed toward Aden and fired missiles at Riyadh, and the Saudi-Houthi truce that held since 2022 is effectively over.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Container lines began edging back toward the Red Sea: a Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab, the canal's southern gate, for the first time in three years. Around it, the Houthis freed 600 fighters as Yemen forces redeployed, and have sent small-arms shipments across the water to Sudan's army.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The tankers Malacca carries start in the Gulf, and that end of the route was where the trouble was: projectiles and mines hit tankers off Khasab on consecutive days, Iran said mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and only 2 liquefied natural gas tankers crossed Hormuz in a week. None of it accounts for more ships through Malacca.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's China news ran through the Trump, Putin and Xi meeting in Shenzhen and the fight over US controls on Nvidia chips. None of it touched shipping through the strait or accounts for its traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones hit 3 ships inside Romanian waters near Sulina, and a wheat ship capsized off Varna after a reported sea-drone strike; all 12 crew survived. Both came after the latest reading, and nothing reported accounts for the line. The EU's von der Leyen pledged €50 million to speed up a Black Sea security hub.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The week before the reading saw Storm Charles shut schools and cancel more than 300 flights in Portugal, and Spain's first general strike in 14 years, which unions say 90% of port workers joined. Nothing in the input ties either event to ships passing through the strait.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: A Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab after three years away, testing the Red Sea shortcut this detour replaced. The same day the Houthis claimed missiles at King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, the kind of threat that keeps most traffic going south, and the seas off the Cape were rough this week.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The strait's news this fortnight came after the last reading. Ukraine's drones hit the Crimean Bridge, a second strike within 24 hours dropped its road span, and satellite imagery later showed hits on the rail span. None of it accounts for the traffic before then.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's Turkish news was a fatal blast at the Habaş steel plant in Aliağa, a defence pact with Qatar, crude flowing again through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline and COP31 in Antalya. None of it bears on the index or explains its slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's data-centre build-out, $94.67 billion of investment approved since 2021, came under scrutiny after the Nvidia scandal, as the U.S. further restricted China's access to AI chips and Anwar's China line triggered a quiet investment freeze from Taiwan. None of the reporting ties those to the index's own companies.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: The fortnight's news from Jakarta was political and monetary. Prabowo was reported to have accepted his Vice President's resignation, the rupiah fell to a record low as Fed bets boosted the dollar, and EU governments signed off on the trade deal with Indonesia. None of these reports ties any of it to the index's slide.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Tokyo's news ran on the yen: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying it, Washington sold $500 million of euros to do the same, and core inflation of 2.2% cemented a rate hike. SoftBank booked over $3 billion in losses on turbine deposits. None of these stories ties itself to the fall in shares.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Company news ran the other way: JD.com returned to profit, Tencent's capital spending jumped 528% under chip curbs, and Alibaba's T-Head chip unit and Adaspace both lined up Hong Kong listings. None of it accounts for the slide in the index.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The fortnight brought producer prices at their highest since June 2022, word from the central bank that China settled nearly 30% of goods trade in yuan, and the Trump–Xi–Putin declaration in Shenzhen; none of it was tied to the slide in Shanghai shares.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: An AI selloff dragged down Samsung and SK Hynix, the two chipmakers the index leans on, in a week when the Nvidia crisis was clouding the chip race. It landed days after SK Hynix began building its first fab in Yongin, a bet on HBM memory for AI.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: India's economic news pulled both ways: October exports jumped 30% and narrowed the trade deficit to $20.09 billion, while retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high that breached the ceiling and put a rate hike in view. Neither story accounts for the index's climb on its own.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's news this fortnight centred on the US criminal probe into Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, and on new US curbs on China's access to AI chips. Nothing reported ties either one to the banks and property firms that weight the index.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Xi pledged Taiwan's reunification without mentioning force, and China staged unannounced Pacific drills the next day that officials called silent intimidation. Nothing reported ties either to this index, and nothing here accounts for the slide or its sharpest single-day fall.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Treasuries sold off on 11 November, when two-year yields jumped 18 basis points overnight on the risk of a half-point Fed hike. That is a jump in global borrowing costs, and it reaches Australian banks and miners. Nothing reported in the period ties the slide to Chinese demand or to a domestic event.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: In Pretoria, 3 of 7 rate-setters voted to hike from 7.25% rather than hold, as inflation risks widened and African economies headed to end the year with high rates while Fed risks loomed. Woolworths Foods turnover grew only 1.9%, a slowdown that hit its shares. Neither accounts for the whole of the slide.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: None of the stories here dates from the slide itself; what followed was a rates and budget story. Brazil's central bank cited four shocks as inflation passed the top of its target range while growth slows, October consumer prices rose 4.63%, below forecasts, and 45 senators passed the government's fiscal adjustment bill.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The retreat from the November peak began when Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans were stopped, after 1,500 migrants set off north from Tapachula. That threat reaches the US demand Mexican firms sell into. A week later the peso hit a 17-month low as the Fed outlook rattled markets.

mkt:byma.standing: Argentina's main stock index, on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos in Buenos Aires. Priced in pesos, which have repeatedly lost most of their value, so it rises even in bad years: daily direction counts, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight's news from Argentina was Pope Leo's visit, whose first papal Mass in 39 years drew 2.5 million people. It also carried Javier Milei's refusal to recognise Lula's election win, and Iran listing Argentina's navy and air force as terrorist organisations. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Carney said only US policy shifts could change Canada's trade stance, ahead of a meeting with Trump in Shenzhen, and the war premium in US sour crude vanished as supply surged. Neither report ties either development to Toronto's slide.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The selloff ran through chipmakers: Nvidia has lost $2.74 trillion in value and Micron 23.6% in a week as investors balked at AI capital spending with no profit in sight. The Fed's Goolsbee left a larger rate rise open for December, 10-year Treasuries yield above 5%, and Trump threatened a tax on US firms' data centres abroad.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight's British news carried UK inflation accelerating again, above target for more than two years; Burnham signing three EU deals with tuition fees left open; and Dangote Cement ending its plan for a London listing. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The slide began the day Mercedes-Benz halted investment in Germany after four months of talks with IG Metall over plant closures. Deutsche Bank shares then fell when a leak of 15 million files showed it had kept about 28,000 flagged clients, and on the day of the low Lufthansa cut 1,000 jobs over fuel costs.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points, and the European Central Bank left France to the markets rather than step in. Ifop polls put Le Pen and Mélenchon ahead of a stalled centre. Protests over rising prices entered a fifth weekend, with 219 arrested on one Saturday.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The Dutch news of the fortnight was the race to replace Christine Lagarde at the ECB, with Knot speaking out as a candidate, and a grid queue of 15,498 Dutch firms waiting for power. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight ran on an election: a general strike over rents, the first in 14 years, then a debate that an Ateneo del Dato poll scored for Feijóo, and Sánchez admitting to mistakes 10 days before the vote. Berlin also conceded Spain the European Central Bank presidency. None of it is tied to the index's slide in the reporting.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's bank news pulled two ways. Italy wants €5.9 billion from its banks next year, a levy Intesa publicly attacked. Brussels gave UniCredit's €45 billion bid for Commerzbank unconditional EU approval. Neither story by itself explains the index's slide.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The latest session's fall came as an AI-led tech selloff sent money into the franc and the yen as havens. A stronger franc shrinks what Swiss companies earn abroad once it is counted back home, so the haven bid for the currency weighs on the index even when its drugmakers and food giants hold up.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The period's news was war and coalition: Israel launched central Gaza's first large operation since the ceasefire, the Board of Peace warned the truce faced collapse, and Eisenkot negotiated with Netanyahu over a unity government. None of the reporting addresses the market or the companies in it.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump met Putin and Xi in Shenzhen at APEC, where the three issued a peace declaration that names no war. In Brooklyn, Asif Merchant got 330 months for plotting to kill him. A Deutsche Bank memo tied two Trump companies to laundromats, and a new order lets firms lose federal contracts for answering Congress without permission.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes after hot inflation; Logan called for two more, and Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open for December. Those bets sent gold to a one-year low, while Trump's panel weighs firing Fed governor Lisa Cook.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: Recent news on the European Central Bank was about who runs it, not what it charges: Christine Lagarde leaves on 7 February, Spain takes the presidency and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier the chief economist seat, while the bank left France to markets as its borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points. None of it explains the rate.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Gold, the metal silver usually trades alongside, had its worst week since March, losing 8.9% as traders bet on a Fed hike after comments from Waller and an AI selloff spread through markets. Spot gold touched $3,757, its lowest since September 2025. None of the reporting addressed silver's own supply or industrial demand.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: October's reading slowed less than expected, and the Fed's Goolsbee called the report "borderline disturbing". Traders took it as cementing bets on a December rate hike: Treasuries slid, gold held a loss near $4,000 and Bitcoin fell to almost a three-month low.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months, and Washington now wants a deal by January 2027. The fighting widened meanwhile: drones hit the Crimean bridge, Russia struck 2 bridges and the subway in Kyiv, and a suspected Russian projectile burned in a Polish field. None of it falls on the spike.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Jensen Huang quit after his ties to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, drew scrutiny and a shareholder lawsuit, leaving Colette Kress as interim CEO. Results that doubled profit to $65.3 billion did not stop the slide, which steepened as it emerged that Commerce had licensed Nvidia chips to military-listed Chinese firms.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple's own news in the fortnight was an outage of its apps and Apple Pay, which it blamed on an internal update as services recovered, and a move into AI agents that control a device while raising new barriers for competitors. Neither accounts for the share's path.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google bought $10 billion of Anthropic in its IPO, and Anthropic then tumbled more than 10% as an AI slump engulfed markets. Google itself shipped its fourth Gemini 4 model in 7 weeks and swapped its homepage Search button for 3 AI buttons, steering users away from the results its ads sit beside.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed 10 minutes after liftoff and destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites. Amazon also said AI agents had found an unpatched flaw themselves, and a study put its 2025 tax rate, like Meta's, under 9%. Nothing reported ties the share's fall to any of it.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: A Microsoft 365 failure left Outlook and Teams disrupted for nearly a day, with Downdetector logging 130,000 Outlook outage reports at the peak, and the shares fell by 3% as offices worldwide lost mail and meetings. In the same week a researcher leaked SignDrop, a Windows exploit that hands ordinary users System rights.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX's tower caught Ship 42, a Starship upper stage, after 14 orbits, and the company laid out $74 billion for AI computing campuses. The European Commission demanded it lift the Starshield limits that cut out Ukraine's interceptor drones. None of it, as reported, accounts for the fall in the share.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: The fortnight brought fines on two fronts: $880m from Italy over photo privacy, and a Brazilian electoral-court penalty for missed court orders. Meta also disclosed that its emissions jumped nearly 40% in 2025 as it built AI data centres. None of it accounts for the price.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Aramco's own assets came under fire: debris from intercepted Houthi missiles blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh, and a day later an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze. A week on, the Yemeni military named Aramco its prime target. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla said it would discontinue the Cybertruck and opened Cybercab orders to select customers, and Bloomberg reported that SpaceX and Tesla may announce a merger in December. Italy then approved its supervised self-driving, rebranded Assisted Driving in Europe, ahead of any EU vote. None of it accounts for the fall.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's Kospi down more than 5% in a single session, during an AI selloff across Asia. The selloff hit hardest at the memory makers, whose chips the AI build-out runs on.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security licensed hundreds of thousands of advanced Nvidia and AMD GPUs to firms the Department of War lists as Chinese military companies. Few of those chips shipped, and Chinese clouds have moved to domestic silicon, so the licences opened little real market. Nothing reported ties them to the share's fall.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Chase went down on Monday, with nearly 5,000 customers reporting outages to Downdetector and Zelle transfers delayed. Three days later hackers took customer data from JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard through a third-party vendor all three share; the banks say nothing sensitive was taken.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: The fall came in an AI selloff aimed at the companies that supply the boom: SK Hynix and Samsung pulled the Kospi down more than 5% in a single session. It came while SK Hynix was building around the clock, 24/7, to finish its first fab in Yongin, a 150-metre-tall plant for the memory that AI chips need.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.
us-mortgage.recent: The one housing story in the window was the result rather than the cause: US home sales fell to their lowest level since 2016, as buyers met borrowing costs well above what most existing owners locked in. Nothing in the input explains the rate's own climb.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The slide ran alongside bitcoin's: it fell below $65,000 for the first time since August, then hit a two-year low before bouncing 9% to retake $60,000. The one Solana-specific item was VanEck dropping Gemini as custodian of its SOL ETF, which does not account for the price.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The fortnight's news put Hyperliquid in the frame as a venue rather than a token: a former Robinhood engineer pleaded guilty to an insider trading scheme run on it, and Nvidia perps crashed there on reports the board may oust Jensen Huang. Neither story accounts for the fall in HYPE.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: UK inflation accelerated to 3.6% in October, leaving it above target for more than two years running. Four days earlier the Bank of England's chief economist said further rate rises were needed to combat inflation, turning the argument from how far to cut to whether to raise.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: The case for another hike built through November. Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen as it slid toward 160 per dollar, and core inflation of 2.2% kept the hike in view despite missing the 2.3% forecast. Against it: Uniqlo reversed a sock price increase within days, a sign shoppers still resist higher prices.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.
tcmb-rate.recent: The one relevant item from the fortnight is the central bank raising its end-2027 inflation forecast to 21%, published after the latest reading. A higher inflation path argues for a slower pace of cuts, but nothing in the input explains the cut itself.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The PBOC spent the fortnight anchoring the yuan with a stable fix as volatility jumped after APEC, and China extended its gold-buying streak to two years; neither involved the lending rate, which the central bank left untouched.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.
bcb-rate.recent: Brazil's central bank is caught between two pressures: inflation has passed the top of its target range while growth slows. The bank names four separate shocks behind the overshoot, so it cannot ease to support a cooling economy without letting prices run further.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.
bi-rate.recent: The latest news on Indonesia's money concerned the currency rather than the rate: the rupiah fell to a record low as Fed bets boosted the dollar, the pressure that limits how far Bank Indonesia can cut. Nothing in it reports a rate decision.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's gold holdings fell to 72.5 million troy ounces in October, the lowest since October 2019, as the National Wealth Fund sold gold to cover a war-swollen budget deficit, and the bank kept buying yuan. None of that accounts for the rate itself, and nothing reported this fortnight explains its path.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Siam Cement said its core Vietnam plastics plant, shut after Hormuz disrupted it, stays closed until mid-2027. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting touches Thai listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's broader slide.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles have reached Riyadh night after night: debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower, an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, and the Houthis claim hitting a Saudi power plant. That hit an Aramco-led index even as Saudi Arabia pumped 10.56 million barrels a day in October, ahead of an OPEC capacity audit.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The gains came in the weeks when Trump signalled that new Iran strikes were unnecessary after a meeting in Qatar, whose PM called the U.S. talks positive. Next door in Abu Dhabi, AD Ports' quarterly profit jumped 73% on shipping rerouted around the Hormuz closure.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's fortnight was dominated by the ASEAN summit, a trade deal Trump announced with the Philippines, and new Quad critical-mineral deals. None of it accounts for the slide in local shares.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Regulators fined it twice in the window: Italy for $880m over photo privacy, and Brazil's electoral court for nine days of missed court orders. It also reconsidered its 2030 net-zero goal after emissions jumped nearly 40% in 2025 on AI data centers. None of this accounts for a fall of this size.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.
poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.recent: The only Spanish story of the period came after the slide had already bottomed out: an Ateneo del Dato poll after the election debate in Madrid found 45% thought Feijóo had won, against 32% for Sánchez. Nothing reported earlier accounts for the drop from late October.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent spent the fortnight on AI. It launched an AI search engine that indexes WeChat accounts, priced Hy4 flash at $0.07 per million input tokens, and reported quarterly capital spending up 528% to 81.4 billion yuan. None of these was reported as the cause of the share's fall.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Jensen Huang left Nvidia after admitting an affair with a Singapore-based company's CEO, amid scrutiny of his ties to Megaspeed, now facing a criminal probe over chip diversion, and shareholders sued alleging they were misled. Results without him doubled profit to $65.3 billion, with a $130bn quarter forecast on Kress's first call.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: The fortnight brought Google's own news but no explanation for the fall: it removed the Search button from its homepage, shipped Gemini 4 Hydrogen and then Gemini Neon, bought $10 billion of Anthropic, and said Android will block apps from unregistered developers from January 2027. None of it accounts for the share price.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: The war came to Saudi soil: an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, the Houthis claimed missiles at King Khalid Airport and a Saudi power plant, and Saudi-led strikes on Hodeidah killed at least 9. Riyadh then sounded emergency alerts a third night running.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, said the 60% uranium stockpile stays home and that Tehran faces a 'major strategic debate' over its nuclear doctrine. The war widened meanwhile: Iran struck Kuwait and Bahrain, and Gharibabadi called the US naval blockade an act of war, even as a Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: The only item in the feed was Obi meeting Plateau traditional rulers, where he decried insecurity, which came after the contract's peak and does not account for the price.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi, but Putin was not ready to make peace there. Within a week he vowed 'much more painful' strikes, as Russia hit Kyiv's bridges and Ukraine's drones struck the Crimean Bridge. Washington's own deadline for a deal, January 2027, falls after this contract closes.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Iran struck Kuwait and Bahrain after a US strike and said mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours in Hormuz. Deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi then called the US naval blockade an act of war and vowed to break it. The one channel still open ran through Qatari mediators in Tehran, not through direct talks.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.
poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.recent: OpenAI's quarterly figures showed an operating loss of $10.9 billion on $10 billion of revenue, which argued against a higher valuation. Nothing reported since accounts for traders paying more for the outcome.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: Iran's Assembly of Experts urged leaving the treaty, Mehr reported. As the war and the US naval blockade went on, Foreign Minister Araghchi spoke of a 'major strategic debate' over nuclear doctrine, while saying the 60% uranium stockpile stays home. In Washington, Vance declined to back Trump's claim that Iran had been close to a bomb.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The war in these weeks was fought from the sea and the air: a US naval blockade, Iranian strikes on Bahrain and Kuwait, and tankers hit and set alight in the Strait of Hormuz, while a Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran on ending it. None of it put US ground forces into Iran, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran struck Kuwait and Bahrain, said mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and a third US carrier reached the Gulf. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi called the blockade an act of war and vowed to break it. A Qatari delegation was in Tehran for talks on ending the war.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: Bettors held off even as Israel launched central Gaza's first large operation since the ceasefire, and the Board of Peace, the truce's overseer, warned it faced imminent collapse. The IDF described its push against a Hamas tunnel that crossed the Yellow Line as a one-day operation and wrapped it up within a day.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on a waterway that Gulf energy exporters and importers depend on.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.recent: Traders paid most for a deal as talks opened, with Iraq carrying a US message and Trump holding strikes at Gulf neighbours' request. The price fell away as tankers were hit off Khasab, Bahrain reported an Iranian strike and Araghchi called reopening the strait irrelevant until Iran's demands are met.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: October's consumer prices rose 0.4%, beating forecasts, and Logan called for two more hikes, possibly rapidly, as two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points. Fed minutes then showed almost all officials expect more hikes. Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open, and a 50 bps move would not pay this quarter-point contract.

poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Ukraine signs its EU accession treaty by 2027. Signing comes only after every negotiating chapter closes and all 27 member states agree, so the price is a bet on the pace of talks in Brussels.
poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.recent: The fortnight's Ukraine news ran to Washington pressing for a peace deal by January 2027, with Kushner saying Moscow appears ready to accept guarantees short of NATO membership, and to an EU proposal for a €45 billion loan repayable only if Russia pays reparations. None of it touched the accession negotiations themselves.

poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Hegseth stops being the US Secretary of Defense before the end of the year. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on reports about his standing at the Pentagon.
poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.recent: The betting peaked when Massie filed 8 impeachment articles against Hegseth, a move that forces a House vote on removing him. Nothing reported since then accounts for traders paying less and less for his exit.

wiki-inflation.standing: The general rise in prices across an economy, usually measured by a consumer price index. Central banks set interest rates to keep it near a target, so its pace decides what borrowers and savers pay.
wiki-inflation.recent: October's price reports ran hot across big economies: US consumer prices rose 0.4%, India's retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high, and China's producer prices reached their highest since June 2022. Fed minutes then showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes. All of these reports came out after the early-month peak, so none of them explains it.

wiki-china.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on China each day: a rough gauge of how often the world's second-largest economy and most populous one-party state pulls general readers toward the basics.
wiki-china.recent: Nothing in the input reaches back to the late-October peak. The fortnight since carried the Shenzhen summit, where Trump, Xi and Putin issued a peace declaration that names no war, a US rule closing an AI chip loophole, and the central bank's figure of nearly 30% of goods trade settled in yuan.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Houthis and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay on the war between Yemen's Houthi movement and the kingdom ending, and so on Red Sea and Gulf oil risk.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: The war moved onto Saudi soil. Houthi strikes hit the East-West pipeline and damaged an Aramco skyscraper in Riyadh, and an attack forced the Asian Cup's postponement. The coalition answered with strikes on Hodeidah and 60 Houthi military sites, the Houthis claimed a Saudi power plant, and Riyadh sounded emergency alerts a third night running.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily reads of English Wikipedia's article on the United States, one of its most-visited country pages. It rises when American power or politics becomes the world's story, not only America's.
wiki-united-states.recent: The fortnight carried air travel chaos that drew a call for Sean Duffy's resignation, uproar over Nvidia chip controls, and Bitcoin's slide below $60,000. None of it accounts for the spike a month earlier.

poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Bola Tinubu wins Nigeria's 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay on a second term for the president of Africa's most populous country.
poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.recent: Wike defended paying N10 million to councillors who deliver wards to Tinubu, Nigeria's electoral commission blamed 54 officials for fake voter records, and a Nasarawa PDP women leader resigned over the party's crisis. None of it is the kind of shock that accounts for what traders pay.

stocks:MSFT.standing: Shares in the maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, one of the world's most valuable companies. Its OpenAI stake and its data-centre spending make it a bellwether for whether the AI build-out pays.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Outlook and Teams were disrupted for nearly a day, with Downdetector logging 130,000 Outlook outage reports at the peak, and the shares fell 3% as the disruption ran on. The same week a researcher leaked SignDrop, a Windows exploit that gives ordinary users System rights.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Iran ceasefire is still holding on 31 December. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on every strike, threat and report of talks.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The contract asks about Israel and Iran, and the fortnight's fire ran between Iran and the US instead: Iran hit Kuwait and Bahrain after a US strike on Qeshm, and a tanker burned near Hormuz. Netanyahu pressed Trump almost daily to resume striking Iran, while Israel's own large operation was in central Gaza.

wiki-nvidia.standing: Nvidia, the Santa Clara chip designer whose graphics processors run most of the world's AI training, and one of the most valuable companies on earth. Its fortunes carry the chip sector and the data-centre build-out with them.
wiki-nvidia.recent: Jensen Huang left Nvidia after emailing staff a confession about an affair with the head of a Singapore-based company, while Megaspeed faced a US criminal probe into chip diversion. Within days Chinese buyers were stockpiling Nvidia chips, Trump backed Huang's return, and Nvidia doubled profit to $65.3 billion without him.

wiki-petroleum.standing: Crude oil and the fuels refined from it: petrol, diesel, jet fuel and the feedstock for plastics. It supplies about a third of the world's energy, and its price runs through transport, food and inflation almost everywhere.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was struck in an attack as Houthi missiles were fired towards Riyadh, yet Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August: Saudi Arabia reported output up 26% in October, and Iraq's Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline pumped crude again after a decade.

poly-will-pete-hegseth-be-the-first-of-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US House of Representatives impeaches Pete Hegseth, the defense secretary, before 2028. Impeachment takes only a simple House majority, so the price lives on who controls the chamber.
poly-will-pete-hegseth-be-the-first-of-t.recent: Traders bid the contract up ahead of a House vote on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's impeachment, then sold it when the chamber shelved the effort 211 to 204. Shelving set the articles aside without impeaching him, and the narrow margin is why the contract kept a price rather than collapsing.

stocks:UAL.standing: The parent of United Airlines, one of the three largest US carriers, with hubs in Chicago, Newark and San Francisco. Its shares move on jet fuel costs, business-travel demand and its transatlantic and Pacific routes.
stocks:UAL.recent: United stopped AI agents such as OpenAI's dots from booking its flights over security concerns. Five days later a widespread system outage stalled its departures for 90 minutes, part of a run of failures at Microsoft, the FAA, Chase and Apple Pay that ended with the White House firing Cairncross.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company Elon Musk founded. It flies most of the world's orbital launches and runs Starlink, the largest satellite internet network, and its military Starshield variant makes it a defence contractor too.
stocks:SPCX.recent: The fortnight's news was about its own business: its tower caught Ship 42 after 14 orbits, it set out plans for $74 billion in AI computing campuses, and Brussels demanded it lift a Starshield cap that cuts off Ukraine's drones above 161 km/h. Nothing in the input ties any of it to the share price.

wiki-jensen-huang.standing: Co-founder of Nvidia, the chipmaker whose graphics processors became the hardware most AI models are trained on. He led it from its founding in 1993, and its rise made him one of the most closely watched executives in technology.
wiki-jensen-huang.recent: Nvidia opened an inquiry into his affair with Alice Huang of Megaspeed, a Singapore company US investigators had watched since 2024 over chip diversion to China. Sen. Cramer called for him to resign, and he quit, leaving finance chief Colette Kress in charge. Trump later backed his return, as 177,000 people petitioned for it.

poly-us-strike-on-cuba-by-december-31.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States carries out a military strike on Cuba before its deadline. Its price is what traders stake on open conflict between Washington and Havana, 90 miles apart across the Florida Straits.
poly-us-strike-on-cuba-by-december-31.recent: In mid-November Trump said he would consider military force against Cuba, the only statement in the fortnight about the outcome this contract settles on. Nothing in the input explains the price's swing in the first days of November, and the bets barely moved after his remark.

stocks:BABA.standing: The Hangzhou group behind Taobao and Tmall, China's biggest online marketplaces, and the country's largest cloud computing business. These New York-listed shares trade on Chinese consumer spending and its bets on artificial intelligence.
stocks:BABA.recent: Nothing Alibaba announced in the fortnight explains the fall. It launched an AI music app that composes and sings a 3-minute song in 1 minute, and said it would keep control of T-Head, its chip unit, after a Hong Kong listing. Over 60% of T-Head's computing serves outside customers.

poly-iaea-visits-isfahan-fordow-or-natan.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors visit an Iranian nuclear site by the year's end. Those inspections are the only outside check on how much enriched uranium Iran holds.
poly-iaea-visits-isfahan-fordow-or-natan.recent: The UN watchdog called on Iran to reopen its facilities, but since the US-Israeli attacks its inspectors cannot reach the sites and do not know where the Isfahan plant is. Tehran moved the other way: the Assembly of Experts urged leaving the nuclear treaty, and the foreign minister said the 60% uranium stockpile stays home.

stocks:1024.HK.standing: Kuaishou runs China's second-largest short-video and live-streaming app after ByteDance's Douyin, and earns from advertising, live-stream tipping and e-commerce. Its shares follow Chinese ad spending and its contest with Douyin.
stocks:1024.HK.recent: Kuaishou is doubling down on Kling, its AI video model, which earned over $20 million in December 2025 alone, while Chinese giants such as Alibaba list AI units in Hong Kong. Neither story explains the fall in the share.

poly-ukraine-signs-peace-deal-with-russi.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a peace deal before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on talks, battlefield turns and Washington's diplomacy.
